_meta.indication: KLISYRI is indicated for the topical treatment of actinic keratosis on the face or scalp.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trial; subjects randomized to KX2-391 (tirbanibulin) ointment 1% or vehicle in a 1:1 ratio.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with 4 to 8 actinic keratosis lesions on the face or scalp.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Complete (100%) clearance rate of AK lesions, i.e., proportion of subjects at Day 57 with no clinically visible AK lesions in the treatment area.
pivotal_trials.result: Complete clearance at Day 57: 44.0% (77/175) tirbanibulin vs 4.5% (8/176) vehicle; treatment difference 39.5% (95% CI 31.6%, 47.5%); p<.0001.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trial; subjects randomized to KX2-391 (tirbanibulin) ointment 1% or vehicle in a 1:1 ratio.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with 4 to 8 actinic keratosis lesions on the face or scalp.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Complete (100%) clearance rate of AK lesions at Day 57 in the treatment area.
pivotal_trials.result: Complete clearance at Day 57: 54.5% (97/178) tirbanibulin vs 12.7% (22/173) vehicle; treatment difference 41.9% (95% CI 33.1%, 50.7%); p<.0001.

key_safety: Adverse reactions were local skin reactions. Application site pain occurred in 6.3% (Study 003) and 13.5% (Study 004) of tirbanibulin subjects vs 3.4% and 2.9% vehicle; application site pruritus in 7.4% and 10.7% vs 4.5% and 7.5% vehicle.
target_moa: Tirbanibulin is a microtubule inhibitor; it binds tubulin, inhibiting tubulin polymerization and disrupting Src tyrosine kinase signaling, disrupting the microtubule network resulting in cell cycle arrest and apoptosis of keratinocytes.

rems.type: No REMS program planned; routine pharmacovigilance and labeling adequate to communicate risks.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was held for this application as there were no complex or substantive review issues.

summary.text: Standard review NDA for a new molecular entity, received December 30, 2019 and approved December 14, 2020; no advisory committee and no REMS. Approval was based on two identical randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled Phase 3 trials.
